judged_text: loadUsers' new catch maps Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError to HttpError 400, rethrowing server-side database failures as client errors with the raw Prisma message. A Prisma known-request error during user loading (e.g. a P2024 connection-pool timeout) reaches booking clients as 400 Bad Request carrying the raw database error text, so clients treat a transient server fault as a permanent request error and internal DB details leak into the response.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed to wrap user-loading logic in a `try/catch` that explicitly maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. This makes server-side/database failures (e.g., connection/pool timeouts) surface as client-side 400 Bad Request and forwards the raw Prisma error message to the client, which is both incorrect error semantics and an information leak. This behavior is directly shown in the added catch block.
